subject: Performance benchmarking scope, access, and acceptance criteria
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@brightdata.ai>, Tom Becker <tom.becker@helixcommerce.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Performance benchmarking scope, access, and acceptance criteria

Hi Elena / Tom —

Thanks again for the conversation this week. Per our MAP, the next gating item for your pilot is the performance benchmarking run so we can validate latency/throughput targets and confirm the acceptance criteria for GA. Outlined below is a concise plan so the team can sign off and we can lock the load windows. Let me know if anything needs to move.

Quick summary (what we want to validate)
- TTFT (time-to-first-token) at p50/p95 under realistic request sizes (1–512 tokens)
- End-to-end latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) for inference pipeline
- Sustained throughput (tokens/sec) at target concurrency (8, 32, 64 concurrent connections)
- Cold-start behavior and KV cache warmup time

Planned logistics
- Test environment: staging.redwood.com (private staging) — we will create a Helix test tenant and API key.
- Test accounts/keys: a short-lived API key + a user-level test account for telemetry.
- Access window: Wed 2026-08-04 22:00 — Thu 2026-08-05 02:00 PDT (4-hour window) and backup window Sat 2026-08-07 02:00 — 06:00 PDT. Please confirm preferred window.
- Load generator: Helix will run existing load harness (Gatling), Redwood will orchestrate servers and provide a runner image and sample traffic traces to replay.

Acceptance criteria (for go/no-go on performance):
- TTFT p95 <= 250 ms for 1–64 token requests; p95 <= 400 ms for 512-token requests
- End-to-end p95 latency for typical requests <= 450 ms (excluding network RTT)
- Sustained throughput >= 40k tokens/sec across the pool at 32 concurrent connections
- No SLA-impacting error spike (error rate < 0.5% over 10-minute intervals)

Attachments: I attached a draft MAP worksheet with milestones and a proposed schedule (redwood_map_v1.xlsx).

Action items
- Elena/Tom: confirm preferred load window and whether Helix will use the internal load harness or Redwood's runner (reply: simple yes/no).
- Rishi/Marissa: I'll need a short-lived API key and a staging tenant created by EOD 2026-08-02.

Thanks —
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(415) 555-0123

From: Elena Morales <elena@brightdata.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Becker <tom.becker@helixcommerce.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 10:04:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Performance benchmarking scope, access, and acceptance criteria

Connor —

Thanks for the clear plan. Helix is good to proceed and the primary ask on our side is to confirm the exact API key permissions and test account retention window (we cannot keep keys longer than 7 days per policy).

A couple of clarifying points:
- We will run our existing Gatling scripts; please supply the traffic traces so we can replay identical distributions.
- For the first run, we prefer the backup window on Sat 2026-08-07 02:00 — 06:00 PDT (less traffic for us).
- Can you confirm the region for the staging work? We need it in us-west-2 to match our egress routing.

Also, Tom asked if Redwood can capture and share per-request KV cache hit-rate during the run (this will help tune warmup).

Elena
Director of Platform Engineering, Helix Commerce
Elena.Morales@brightdata.ai

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@brightdata.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Tom Becker <tom.becker@helixcommerce.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 31 Jul 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance benchmarking scope, access, and acceptance criteria

Elena —

Thanks — confirmed:
- Staging region will be us-west-2.
- We'll provision a Helix test tenant on staging and issue a short-lived API key (valid 7 days). Key will be scoped to inference-only and telemetry read.
- Redwood will provide the load runner Docker image and the exact request traces (same JSON payloads we discussed) in the Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cMAPPlan

Regarding KV cache metrics: yes — we will surface per-request cache hit/miss and a running warmup profile (minute-resolution) in the run logs. We'll also capture TTFT and per-token throughput. We'll upload aggregated CSVs and raw logs as benchmark-run-logs.tar.gz.

Proposed detailed schedule (actionable milestones that I'll add to the MAP worksheet):
1) 2026-08-02: staging tenant + API key created; access validation by Helix (smoke test) — owner: Rishi/Marissa
2) 2026-08-05 22:00 PDT: primary run (4 hrs) — owner: Helix (run), Redwood (monitor & collect logs)
3) 2026-08-07 02:00 PDT: backup run — owner: same as above
4) 2026-08-09: Redwood provides benchmark summary + MAP entry with pass/fail for acceptance criteria — owner: Connor/Rishi

I'll prepare the brief runbook (commands, docker image, environment variables) and drop it in the Drive folder by EOD 2026-08-02.

Rishi Malhotra
Head of Performance Engineering, Redwood Inference

From: Tom Becker <tom.becker@helixcommerce.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Morales <elena@brightdata.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance benchmarking scope, access, and acceptance criteria

On Fri, Jul 31, 2026 at 09:18 AM Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com> wrote:
> Elena —
> 
> Thanks — confirmed:
> - Staging region will be us-west-2.
> - We'll provision a Helix test tenant on staging and issue a short-lived API key (valid 7 days). Key will be scoped to inference-only and telemetry read.
> - Redwood will provide the load runner Docker image and the exact request traces (same JSON payloads we discussed) in the Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cMAPPlan
> 
> Regarding KV cache metrics: yes — we will surface per-request cache hit/miss and a running warmup profile (minute-resolution) in the run logs. We'll also capture TTFT and per-token throughput. We'll upload aggregated CSVs and raw logs as benchmark-run-logs.tar.gz.

Thanks all — confirmed on our side. Per the acceptance criteria, we'd like Redwood to also provide a short comparison table in the MAP showing current prod baseline (our internal numbers) vs. staging run results so the PO can sign the performance section. If you can model a simple delta table in the MAP (p50/p95 TTFT, p95 latency, sustained tokens/sec) that covers 1–512 token workloads, that will speed approval.

We'll run the backup window on Sat 2026-08-07 02:00 PDT. Please share the API key when ready (secure transfer), and ping me once the runbook is uploaded.

Thanks —
Tom Becker
VP Engineering, Helix Commerce
